description.narrative: The IFC is considering an US$11 million corporate finance package to Djeliba Leisure Group (DLG), a group comprised of four Gambian companies acting as co-borrowers - Djeliba Leisure Group Ltd, Balafon Company Ltd, EON Company Ltd, and International Tourism Investment Ltd to support hotel expansion, refurbishment, and energy efficiency improvements. The financing comprises an IFC A-Loan and a subordinated loan from International Development Association Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) and the Concessional Capital Window (CCW). Proceeds will support a US$20.76 million investment program across four beachfront hotels in The Gambia: Balafon Beach Resort; Kombo Beach Resort; TUI BLUE Tamala hotel; and Kalimba Beach Resort. Djeliba Leisure Group Ltd. Use of financing proceeds will cover construction of new rooms and room refurbishment across the four hotels; upgrades to employee welfare facilities; and installation of a 1.5MW solar photovoltaic (PV) system with battery energy storage to supply solar power exclusively for on-site hotel operations at three hotels. All four hotels are expected to receive EDGE certification.

The project is expected to generate economy wide benefits through both direct and indirect job creation and contributions to GDP; employment impacts through the creation of high quality jobs in hotel operations; and environmental gains in the form of energy and water savings, as well as reductions in GHG emissions, achieved through the green certification of hotel assets. The employment impact is also inclusive, reflecting the clients commitment to significantly increase the proportion of female employees. In addition, IFC anticipates that the investment will strengthen competitiveness in the hospitality sector, particularly in the mid to upscale segment, by fostering competitive pressure. It will support the clients a shift away from a mass sun, sea, and sand tourism model toward a more diversified, higher value offering, with strong potential for replication and scale up within the local market by other players.
